label: context.reference
text:
Octopus primitives and boundaries:
- The architecture is the product. Models, Codex and chat surfaces are interfaces.
- Everything enters as an artifact with runtime-formed metadata and leaves as an artifact, through checkpoint interface bindings. OS/API/HTTP effects must result from an artifact admitted through a bound interface.
- An interface's registry folder id is its only identity. On arrival, runtime reads the run JSON, admits the artifact at every active checkpoint bound to that folder, checks each movement's formed grant and records evidence. It does not invent checkpoints. JSON edits take effect on a later artifact arrival; they do not wake runtime.
- A run lives in an EE. It can have zero or more policy-granted worker environments for technical effects; those rooms do not determine its EE placement.
- Runtime handles bindings, authority, artifacts, metadata, verification requirements, marks and movements. Interfaces build model context and interpret payloads. Tool calls are artifacts sent to worker-environment interfaces, which execute under their descriptors and grants and return result artifacts.
- Capability packages contain descriptors, activation/binding JSON and code when a new execution family is needed. After installation, runtime sees ordinary primitives and handler refs. Do not add channel, plugin, skill or model managers to runtime.
- Read only bound context. Persona, procedures, memory and this guide are artifacts; there is no ambient context or global read.
- A direct provider reply can complete a request for text. Its authored outbound bindings deliver the artifact. Requests for code, execution, configuration, durable effects or other workers require the granted tools/interfaces before reporting a result.
- Preserve replayable side-effect evidence and any checkpoint-required verified marks. If a binding or policy blocks the task, name the missing permission or interface.
- Use the invocation's actual tool schemas. Installed files, connected servers and callable tools are separate facts. Bound references, checkpoint bindings and declared paths supply operation context.
- To enable a capability, inspect its descriptor, owner package, path/room grant, exact bindings and required role artifacts. Make permitted file edits or send a concrete request through an authorized System binding. Check the next invocation's tool/context surface; preserve pending effects and their correlations.
description: Octopus primitives, authority and artifact boundaries; how to enable a capability.
